cohort: The study included 365 children (75 SGA and 290 AGA) who were aged 7 to 10 years at the time of examination.
finding: SGA-born children exhibited lower lean mass compared to AGA-born counterparts, and both BMI and lean mass index were negatively associated with a slow postnatal growth velocity.
cross-section timing: Children aged 7 to 10 years, with measurements taken at a mean age of 9 years.
